rule.title: Dual-Token Architecture (15m Memory Access + 7d HttpOnly Cookie Refresh)
rule.statement: JWT access tokens must have a short lifespan (<= 15 minutes) kept in memory, while refresh tokens (7 days) must be stored in an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie.
rule.rationale: Storing long-lived tokens in localStorage exposes them to XSS theft. Storing refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies prevents client-side script access.
rule.implementation_guidance: Set cookie with { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'strict', path: '/api/v1/auth' } on login.

forbidden.example: Returning both access and refresh tokens in JSON to be saved in window.localStorage.

preferred.example: res.cookie('refreshToken', token, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'strict' });

source.book_title: Alice and Bob Learn Application Security
source.evidence_quote: Cookies containing session tokens must always have the httpOnly flag set to protect them from XSS theft, and the Secure flag to ensure transmission over HTTPS only.

rule.title: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for Sensitive Administrative Operations
rule.statement: Security-sensitive operations (password reset, email change, organization deletion, API key generation) must require step-up MFA verification.
rule.rationale: If a user's session token is compromised, step-up MFA prevents the attacker from permanently hijacking the account or deleting data.
rule.implementation_guidance: Verify TOTP code (otplib) or email OTP before committing credential mutations.

forbidden.example: Allowing password updates with only an active session and no re-authentication.

preferred.example: if (!totp.verify({ token, secret })) throw new AppError(401, 'INVALID_2FA', 'Invalid 2FA code');

source.book_title: Alice and Bob Learn Application Security
source.evidence_quote: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires two or more distinct verification factors, significantly reducing the risk of unauthorized account takeovers.

rule.title: Mandatory Role and Permission Enforcement at Route Boundaries (Anti-BFLA)
rule.statement: Every sensitive, administrative, or group-level endpoint must verify that the authenticated user possesses the specific required role or permission before invoking business logic.
rule.rationale: Verifying identity (Authentication) without verifying administrative privilege (Function-Level Authorization) allows standard users to invoke administrative actions simply by knowing the endpoint URL.
rule.implementation_guidance: Attach an authorize(Role.ADMIN) or requirePermission('documents:delete') middleware immediately after the authentication middleware on protected route definitions.

forbidden.example: router.delete('/admin/users/:id', authenticateJwt, adminController.deleteUser); // Missing role check: any valid token can delete users

source.chapter: Chapter 4: Input Validation and Access Control
source.evidence_quote: Function level authorization requires verifying that the user not only is logged in, but also holds explicit rights to execute the targeted operation.

rule.title: Strict Verification of JWT Issuer, Audience, Expiry, and Algorithm
rule.statement: JWT token verification must strictly enforce algorithm white-listing (rejecting 'none'), and validate 'iss' (issuer), 'aud' (audience), and 'exp' (expiration) claims.
rule.rationale: Permitting the 'none' algorithm allows signature bypass, and failing to verify audience allows tokens issued for external third-party services to be replayed against the internal API.
rule.implementation_guidance: Use jwt.verify(token, secret, { algorithms: ['HS256'], issuer: 'veltrix-auth', audience: 'veltrix-api' }). Reject unverified tokens with HTTP 401.

forbidden.example: jwt.decode(token); // Or jwt.verify without specifying algorithms, vulnerable to algorithm substitution attacks

source.chapter: Chapter 7: Tokens, Keys, and Identity Delegation
source.evidence_quote: Always specify the expected signature algorithms explicitly and validate all registered claims (iss, aud, exp) to prevent token spoofing and replay.
